title: User wants an instant fix, queue has priorities
symptom: User demands his ticket is fixed before others
user_description: I need my problem fixed right now! I've been waiting an hour and my ticket should be at the top.

options.text: Promise it will be done in ten minutes
options.why: A promise you cannot keep makes things worse when it is broken.

options.text: Tell him there is nothing you can do
options.why: Unhelpful. A good technician explains the process and offers a way forward.

options.text: Move the ticket to the top without asking anyone
options.why: Skips the priority process and is unfair to others who may have more serious problems.

options.text: Explain how tickets are prioritised, ask whether there is business impact that changes it, give an honest timeframe, and keep him updated
options.why: Explaining the process shows fairness. Asking about impact may reveal a reason to raise the priority, and honest updates keep trust.

hints: Might something about his problem change its priority?
What does an honest answer sound like?
real_world_tip: Ask 'What is the impact if this isn't fixed in the next hour?' It turns frustration into facts.
